chief_complaint.text: Fever, cough, body pain, and fatigue.

history_of_present_illness.text: Patient presents with fever, cough, body pain, and fatigue for 3 days. Fever was initially mild, then spiked to 101 °F yesterday evening. Took Paracetamol 650 mg twice yesterday, which temporarily reduced fever. Cough is mostly dry, occasionally with a little mucus. Patient reports slight breathlessness on climbing stairs. Denies chest pain, wheezing, severe shortness of breath, loss of smell or taste, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, or burning during urination. Patient had contact with an office colleague who had a viral fever last week.
items: Took Paracetamol 650 mg twice yesterday with temporary relief
Denies wheezing or severe shortness of breath
Denies loss of smell or taste
Denies abdominal pain or burning during urination
Contact history with office colleague with viral fever last week

past_history.text: History of Hypertension, diagnosed 5 years ago, on Amlodipine 5 mg once daily. No history of diabetes, asthma, thyroid disease, surgeries, or previous hospital admissions.

family_history.text: Father has diabetes. Mother has hypertension.

drug_allergy.text: Allergic to Penicillin, develops a skin rash after taking it.

clinical_examination.text: Current vitals: Temperature 100.8 °F, BP 132/84 mmHg, Pulse 92/min, SpO2 98%, Weight 74 kg. Patient appears conscious, oriented, mildly febrile, and not in respiratory distress. No swelling or rashes noted. Respiratory system appears mildly affected with an upper respiratory tract infection. No concerning cardiac, abdominal, or neurological symptoms are present from history.
items: No concerning cardiac, abdominal, or neurological symptoms
clinical_examination.general_examination: Conscious, oriented, mildly febrile, not in respiratory distress. No swelling or rashes.
clinical_examination.systemic_examination: Respiratory system appears mildly affected with an upper respiratory tract infection. No concerning cardiac, abdominal, or neurological symptoms are present from history.

diagnosis.text: Provisional diagnosis: Acute viral upper respiratory tract infection (viral fever with pharyngitis).
items: Acute viral upper respiratory tract infection

investigations.text: Investigations are advised only if fever continues beyond 48 hours or symptoms worsen. These include Complete Blood Count (CBC), C-reactive protein (CRP), COVID-19 or influenza test (if indicated), and Chest X-ray (if breathlessness increases).
items: Investigations only if fever > 48 hours or symptoms worsen

prescription.text: Tablet Paracetamol 650 mg, one tablet every 6 hours if fever exceeds 100°F (maximum 4 tablets per day). Continue Amlodipine 5 mg once daily. Tablet Levosteirizine 5 mg, once daily at night for 5 days.
items: Paracetamol 650 mg, 1 tablet every 6 hours if fever > 100°F (max 4 tablets/day)
Levosteirizine 5 mg, 1 tablet OD at night for 5 days

advice.text: Perform warm saline gargles 3-4 times daily and steam inhalation twice daily. Drink plenty of fluids, get adequate rest, and eat soft nutritious food. Wear a mask if you're around family members to reduce transmission. Keep a record of your temperature and oxygen saturation twice daily. Seek emergency care immediately if you develop difficulty breathing, persistent high fever above 102°F, oxygen saturation below 94%, severe chest pain or confusion.
items: Wear a mask around family members to reduce transmission

Seek emergency care immediately if: difficulty breathing, persistent high fever > 102°F, oxygen saturation < 94%, severe chest pain, or confusion.

follow_up.text: Review after 3 days or earlier if symptoms worsen.
